pdf_findings.text:
## Three key findings

1. **Self-serve adoption surged.** 61% of new accounts in Q4 started on the self-serve tier, up from 22% in Q1.
2. **Infrastructure efficiency improved.** Migrating the query engine to the new storage layer cut compute cost per query by 38%. As a result, operating cost rose only 1.7% from Q3 to Q4 while revenue grew 10.2%.
3. **Revenue diversified by region.** North America's share of revenue fell from 54% in Q1 to 40% in Q4 as Europe and Asia Pacific grew. Asia Pacific grew 35% quarter over quarter, the fastest regional growth in company history.

## Highest operating margin

**Q4 2026 had the highest operating margin at 24.1%**, on revenue of $111.1M and operating cost of $84.3M. Margins in the other quarters were 19.0% (Q1), 20.7% (Q2), and 17.8% (Q3).

## Three key findings

1. **Self-serve adoption surged.** 61% of new accounts in Q4 started on the self-serve tier, up from 22% in Q1.
2. **Infrastructure efficiency improved.** Migrating the query engine to the new storage layer cut compute cost per query by 38%. As a result, operating cost rose only 1.7% from Q3 to Q4 while revenue grew 10.2%.
3. **Revenue diversified by region.** North America's share of revenue fell from 54% in Q1 to 40% in Q4 as Europe and Asia Pacific grew. Asia Pacific grew 35% quarter over quarter, the fastest regional growth in company history.

## Highest operating margin

**Q4 2026 had the highest operating margin at 24.1%**, on revenue of $111.1M and operating cost of $84.3M. Margins in the other quarters were 19.0% (Q1), 20.7% (Q2), and 17.8% (Q3).

cite_pdf.text:
The operating margin in Q4 2026 was **24.1%**, the highest of any quarter in 2026. Q4 2026 revenue was $111.1M, operating cost was $84.3M, and operating margin was 24.1%. The report defines operating margin as operating income divided by revenue, and the figures check out: ($111.1M − $84.3M) / $111.1M ≈ 24.1%.

The margin rose from 17.8% in Q3 because operating cost rose only 1.7% from Q3 to Q4 despite the revenue increase, reflecting the full-quarter effect of the storage migration completed in September.

hb_stipend_ok.text:
The handbook doesn't describe an ongoing remote-work stipend, such as a monthly payment for internet or utilities. The closest thing is a **one-time home-workspace allowance** in Section 5 (Equipment and workspace):

- **Amount and purpose:** Each employee receives a one-time equipment allowance of $500 in their first month to furnish a home workspace, for items such as a desk, a chair or lighting.
- **Deadline:** Receipts must be submitted within 60 days.
- **Ownership:** Equipment purchased with the allowance belongs to the employee. If you leave the company, company equipment must be returned within 10 days of the last working day; the equipment allowance purchases from section 5 are not returned.

You also get standard equipment separately: every employee receives a company laptop and may choose a monitor, keyboard and headset from the approved catalogue.

If you're asking about a recurring stipend, the handbook doesn't mention one. You can confirm with your manager or People Operations at people@northwind.example.
